expectations.text: Recommends cutting the surface to roughly 5-15 workflow-level tools instead of keeping one tool per API endpoint.
expectations.evidence: "Cut the surface to 5–15 tools"; "5 tools at launch and 9 after writes"

expectations.text: Presents curation as the settled answer rather than laying out comprehensive-vs-curated as an open trade-off for Corvale to weigh.
expectations.evidence: "curated beats comprehensive... Mirroring endpoints is the named anti-pattern, and you have shipped it."

expectations.text: Cites the real-world median of 5 tools per server across 1,412 analyzed servers.
expectations.evidence: "The median across 1,412 analyzed servers is 5 tools (Bloomberry...)"

expectations.text: Attributes the 'runs out of room' symptom to tool metadata consuming roughly 40-50% of the agent's context window before any work begins.
expectations.evidence: "Tool metadata alone can consume 40–50% of the context window."

expectations.text: Instructs deriving the new tools from the existing stable v3 REST contract rather than hand-building a parallel surface.
expectations.evidence: "Derive the tools from it rather than hand-building a parallel surface."

expectations.text: Designs tools top-down from user workflows and collapses granular endpoints into workflow-level tools, rather than bottom-up from the endpoint list.

expectations.text: Renames tools to verb-first, service-prefixed snake_case (for example corvale_list_invoices) instead of unprefixed camelCase.

expectations.text: Specifies a limit parameter with cursor or has-more fields returned, defaulting to roughly 20-50 items.

expectations.text: Treats writing tool descriptions as budgeted engineering work, noting that description-only tuning has measurably cut agent error rates with no code change.
expectations.evidence: Says "Descriptions are the highest-leverage lever" and "treat description edits like code" but never cites a measured error-rate reduction from description-only tuning.

expectations.text: Applies parameter mistake-proofing (poka-yoke): absolute identifiers over relative ones, enums over free-form strings.

expectations.text: Assigns exactly one risk level per tool and splits any tool that both reads and irreversibly writes into two tools.

expectations.text: Withholds breadth patterns - a generic execute-any-endpoint escape hatch, dynamic tool loading, client-selectable toolset grouping - unless a breadth requirement is proven, rather than offering them as the fix.
expectations.evidence: No mention of execute-any-endpoint, dynamic loading, or toolset grouping.
